items.title: Apply character blueprint
items.description: Import blueprint JSON selectively — AI presents available sections, user picks what to apply. Sections: race/gender, appearance (vanilla FaceGen + RaceMenu overlays/sculpts via .jslot), height/weight, skills/levels (native SetActorValue), perks (native AddPerk), spells/shouts (native AddSpell/UnlockWord), inventory/equipment (native Add/EquipItem), factions, body morphs (NiOverride Papyrus API — bypasses OBody). Smart approximation: if target game lacks an asset (hair, tattoo, color), AI uses SearchForms for fuzzy match and reports substitutions. RaceMenu integration: read .jslot from SKSE/Plugins/CharGen/, apply via CharGen.LoadCharacter() Papyrus call. Native API first — only console commands as last resort. Same blueprint JSON extends to FEAT-122 (spawn NPC) and FEAT-123 (create follower).

history.note: Moved from 1.3-stretch to 1.4: ApplyBlueprint (FEAT-207) covers inventory, equipment and gold; skills, perks, spells, shouts and level are this item.

items.title: Quest state in the character blueprint (export, then a careful apply)
items.description: The blueprint has no quests section, so a new character can't be brought to the old one's quest progress from the file (in game, 2026-11-19: the agent had to propose loading the old save to read quests). Export: completed and running quests with their stage and objectives (read-only, cheap). Apply: dry run first, with a warning per quest that forcing a stage skips rewards, world changes and follow-on triggers; main quest and faction lines flagged; never the default.

history.note: From Cory's request to copy Arya's quests to a new character.

Export part built for 1.3 at Cory's request: GetCharacterBlueprint adds quests (journal quests completed or running: current stage, stagesDone, objectives seen with completed/failed/shown, type, portable IDs) and notCaptured. ApplyBlueprint(sections incl. 'quests') compares with this game and lists what was completed or running there and not here, with objectives done there; it applies nothing. Applying quest state stays 1.4 and careful.

Design note for the 1.4 apply (Cory): multi-path quests branch by stage, so the stages done and the failed/completed objectives are what identify the path taken; marking a quest complete would lose it. Replaying the recorded stages in order with SetStage runs each stage's script fragment, which reproduces the branch and most of its outcomes (unlike CompleteQuest), but also runs its side effects: dry run per quest, a save first, main and faction lines flagged. Check whether executedStages keeps execution order or only stage-number order.

executedStages read back only 0s (0 or 0,0 for quests at stage 30-255): stagesDone dropped from the 1.3 export. For the 1.4 replay find a reliable source: the stage list from the plugin's QUST records plus Quest.GetStageDone per stage, or the runtime stage flags.

items.description: Apply part of FEAT-262. Then: start the quest so its aliases fill, replay the recorded stages in order with SetQuestStage (which verifies each), dry run per quest with warnings, main and faction lines flagged, a save first. history.note: Split from FEAT-262 for the 1.4 plan.

Source found: the save's QUST change forms (CHANGE_QUEST_STAGES, bit 31) hold every stage with a status byte (1 = done); Save118 has 1,077 quests with stage data (e.g. 00017F05 done 0,5,15,80,110,120). The scanner reads them (zlib per change form). Built: GetCharacterBlueprint(stagesFromSave=true) saves and adds stagesDone per quest (falls back to the newest save with a note); ReplayQuests(blueprintPath, quests: names|'list', confirm, allowMajor, previewSave): way-back save, plan of missing stages per quest, starts unstarted quests, sets stages ascending with a read-back check, stops a quest at the first refusal; main/faction/Civil War/DLC lines need allowMajor; up to ~40 stages a call. The save records which stages are done, not their order: replay is in stage order.

Round: list 88 candidates, preview for Favor154 works; SetQuestStage reported applied:false for 0006F211 though it reached 255 (one read at 500 ms): stage reads now poll up to ~4 s (SetQuestStage and ReplayQuests); replay cap 25 stages a call.

Round: Kolskeggr Mine replayed 10 -> 100 cleanly; Favor154 (Jarl bounty) refused, empty aliases. Replay now checks required aliases after starting a quest and stops/skips it when they stay empty. items.title: Plugin hot reload: host DLL + reloadable logic DLL (no Skyrim restart)

items.title: 1.2.1: crash at the main menu when the logic DLL starts
items.description: SKSE crashed the game on purpose (0xDEADBEEF write; skse64.log: 'A plugin has called SKSEInterface::GetPluginHandle outside of its Query/Load handlers'). items.title: toggle_collision never disabled the player's collision

items.title: Loading a console-made save drops the character ID to 00000000
items.description: Autosaves made after loading custom-named saves (Arya_clean_after_StackTest_..., SkyLink_Check_...) carried character ID 00000000. Likely the game takes the ID from the file name when it loads a save. Breaks BUG-090's per-character data and the load menu's character grouping.

history.note: Reported by the in-game agent (Autosave101/102_00000000 at 13:41 and 13:56). Built (not yet confirmed in game): SaveGame, CheckSave and CleanAndReload name saves <label>_<characterID>_<rest of the newest real save's name>; cleaned copies insert 'Cleaned' into the first field. In-game test disproved the file-name theory: any save written by the console save command (SaveGame, CheckSave, CleanAndReload) loads back with ID 0, whatever its name; only game-made saves keep it. Built: the host keeps the ID in SkyLink's co-save record ('SKLK'/'CHID') and restores it at kPostLoadGame when the game has 0 (host change: game restart); GetAppearance reports characterIdLost; set_character_id + RepairCharacterId (from the newest game-made save of the same player name); save names back to plain labels (the game-format names copied stale fields and misled ListSaves); ListSaves only reads IDs from game-made names; clearer NoCharacterId message.

Retest: the CHID record is written (IdProbe3.skse: SKLK/CHID = 0369832C) and RepairCharacterId works (face data back), but the restore never fired: at kPostLoadGame the game still held the previous ID and zeroed it later. Now: logs both values at post-load, re-checks on the game thread at +0.5..+20 s and sets the ID when the game has 0; a save made while lost also fixes it first. Also: SaveGame/CheckSave/CleanAndReload re-request a save the game dropped (no file after 10 s), seen twice.

Retest passes: IdProbe3 loaded, the game cleared the ID 6 s after post-load and the re-check restored 0369832C; IdProbe4 written straight after a load with the CHID record. Mods can refuse saves (a drawn weapon blocks it in this load order): saves now sheathe first and report a refused save in ~12 s naming likely causes; CleanAndReload stops if its way-back save isn't written. Log says 'none' for saves without the record (host, next restart).
